title: Celebrations
specPoints: My personal world: customs and festivals

tips.title: Fêter, célébrer, offrir
tips.body: *On **fête** Noël en famille. On **célèbre** l'Aïd. J'**offre** un cadeau à ma sœur.* *Fêter* and *célébrer* both mean to celebrate; **offrir** is to give a present (*donner* is just to hand over). *Offrir* is irregular: *j'offre, nous offrons*, and its participle is **offert**.

tips.title: Dates: le + number + month
tips.body: *Noël, c'est **le 25 décembre**.* No *of*, no capital on the month, and the number is ordinary — except the first, which is **le premier**: *le premier janvier*. *En décembre* for the month alone, *le 25 décembre* for the date.

tips.title: Chez for someone's house
tips.body: *On va **chez** ma grand-mère. On se retrouve **chez** moi.* *Chez* + a person is *at their house* — never *à la maison de*. It is the natural word for where a family celebration happens.

tips.title: Traditionnellement, d'habitude, cette année
tips.body: *D'habitude on reste à la maison, mais **cette année** on est allés en France.* A usual custom in the **present**, this year's event in the **perfect** — one sentence, two tenses, and the grammar the topic is really testing.

tips.title: Il y a to describe the day
tips.body: *Il y a un grand repas, il y a des feux d'artifice, il y a de la musique.* *Il y a* + noun lists what happens at a festival without needing a new verb each time, and *des* becomes *de* after a negative: *il n'y a pas **de** cadeaux*.

why.matters: Christmas, Eid, a birthday, a wedding: everyone has celebrations, which makes them the safest subject for a picture task and the reason the topic exists. It teaches the shape of a French date, *le 14 juillet*, with a small letter on the month and *le premier* for the first, and it is built to be told in three tenses: what usually happens in the present, what happened last year in the perfect, what is going to happen this year in the near future. The festivals of France come with it, so that a text about *la fête nationale* is not a mystery.

examples.title: The date on the invitation
examples.body: A French invitation says *le 25 décembre* or *le premier mai*, and the shape never changes: *le*, the number, the month with no capital letter. Only the first of the month is written as an ordinal; every other day is a plain number, so *le deux mai* rather than a second. The pattern is worth learning cold because dates are in every listening paper, and a date is the kind of detail a question turns on.

visual.alt: A table of four dates written the French way, with le, the number and the month in lower case, and le premier for the first of the month

examples.title: Three tenses at one party
examples.body: The same celebration can be told three ways, and the mark scheme rewards all three in one answer. *D'habitude on mange chez ma grand-mère* is the custom, present tense. *L'année dernière on est allés au restaurant* is what happened, perfect. *Cette année on va inviter mes cousins* is the plan, near future. The time marker at the front of each sentence fixes the tense before the verb arrives, so the examiner sees the range before reading a word of the verb.

visual.alt: A table of a celebration told in three tenses, the custom in the present, last year in the perfect and this year in the near future, each announced by its time marker

examples.title: What there was on the day
examples.body: Describing last year's celebration needs two verbs that never change: *il y avait* for what there was, *c'était* for what it was like. *Il y avait un repas, un feu d'artifice et des décorations partout; c'était magnifique.* Neither agrees with anything, so they are safe, and they are the background against which the perfect-tense events happen. The listening paper describes a party this way, and a candidate who knows *il y avait* has the scene before the questions start.

steps.title: Les fêtes
steps.body:
Festivals are **nouns with dates**, and French gives the date in a fixed shape.

**The date**: *le* + number + month, no capital on the month: *le 25 décembre, le 14 juillet, le 31 octobre*. The **first** of a month is *le **premier***: *le premier janvier, le premier mai*.

**The festivals** a GCSE text uses: *le Nouvel An* (New Year), *la fête des Rois* (Epiphany), *la Saint-Valentin, Pâques* (Easter), *la fête du Travail* (1 May), *la fête nationale* (14 July, also called *le quatorze juillet*), *la Toussaint* (All Saints, 1 November), *Noël* (Christmas), *le Ramadan, l'Aïd, Diwali, Hanoukka*, *un mariage* (a wedding), *un anniversaire* (a birthday).

**The verbs**: *on **fête** Noël*, *on **célèbre** l'Aïd*, *on **organise** une fête* (organise a party), *on **invite** la famille*, *j'**offre** un cadeau* (give a present — *offrir*, participle **offert**).

**What happens** — *il y a* + noun: *il y a un grand repas, un défilé* (a parade), *un feu d'artifice* (fireworks), *de la musique, des décorations, des cadeaux*.

**Where**: *chez ma grand-mère, chez nous, à la maison, en ville, dans la rue*.

steps.title: Ce qu'on fait d'habitude
steps.body:
A custom is a **habit**, so it goes in the **present tense** with a frequency phrase.

**Habit markers**: *d'habitude* (usually), *normalement, traditionnellement, tous les ans* (every year), *chaque année, en général*.

*D'habitude, on fête Noël chez ma grand-mère. Tous les ans, on prépare un grand repas. Traditionnellement, on offre des cadeaux le matin.*

**On** is the everyday *we* and takes the *il* ending: *on fête, on mange, on offre, on se réunit* (we get together — reflexive).

**The food**: *on mange de la dinde* (turkey), *une bûche de Noël* (Christmas log), *des crêpes, un gâteau, des chocolats*; *on boit du champagne, du jus de fruit*.

**Time of day**: *le matin, à midi, le soir, à minuit* (midnight), *toute la journée* (all day), *jusqu'à deux heures du matin*.

**Who comes**: *toute la famille, mes cousins, mes grands-parents, les voisins* (neighbours). *Il y a environ vingt personnes* — 12 family and 8 friends is 20.

**Opinions**: *j'adore cette fête parce que…, c'est mon jour préféré, c'est l'occasion de voir toute la famille* (it is a chance to…).

steps.title: Trois temps dans une réponse
steps.body:
The best celebration answers move between **three tenses**, because a festival has a custom, a last time and a next time.

**Present — the custom**: *tous les ans, on fête Noël chez nous*.

**Perfect — last year**: *l'année dernière, on est allés en France et on a mangé une bûche*.

**Near future — this year**: *cette année, on va inviter les voisins et je vais offrir un cadeau à ma sœur*.

**Two useful imperfect forms**: *il y **avait*** (there was / were) and *c'**était*** (it was). *Il y avait beaucoup de monde* (a lot of people), *c'était super*. They set the scene and give the opinion without the whole imperfect tense.

**Negatives across tenses**: *on ne fête pas Halloween*, *je n'ai pas reçu de cadeaux* (*des → de*), *on ne va pas sortir*.

**Comparing customs**: *en France, on fête le 14 juillet, mais en Angleterre on ne le fête pas*; *chez nous, c'est différent*; *comme en France* (like in France).

**Linking**: *d'abord, ensuite, après, enfin*; *par contre* (on the other hand); *ce que j'aime le plus, c'est …* (what I like most is…).

steps.title: Your turn
steps.body:
**Part A.**

1. Write the dates of three festivals in French, including one *le premier*.
2. Translate: *we celebrate Christmas at my grandmother's house.*
3. Write three things there are at a festival with *il y a*.

**Part B.**

4. Describe your usual custom in the present with *d'habitude*.
5. Say what you did last year in the perfect.
6. Say what you are going to do this year in the near future.

**Part C.**

7. Write a sentence with *il y avait* and one with *c'était*.
8. Compare a French custom with one in your country.
9. Write a paragraph of six sentences about your favourite celebration, using the present, the perfect and the near future.

For question 9, check that each time marker matches the tense after it.

visuals.alt: A blank five-row table for the student to build a paragraph about a celebration in three tenses

steps.title: Going deeper
steps.body:
**Get the date shape right.** *Le 25 décembre, le premier mai.* No capital on the month, *le premier* for the first, and no *de*.

**Match the tense to the marker.** *D'habitude* → present; *l'année dernière* → perfect; *cette année / demain* → near future. Mismatching them is the error that costs most here, because the whole topic is built on the contrast.

**Use chez.** *Chez ma grand-mère, chez nous, chez des amis.* Compact and native.

**Add il y avait and c'était.** *Il y avait une centaine de personnes et c'était bruyant mais génial.* Two imperfect forms give you description in the past without a new tense.

**Shrink the article after a negative.** *Je n'ai pas reçu **de** cadeaux; on ne mange pas **de** viande.*

**Use offrir properly.** *J'offre un cadeau **à** ma sœur* → *je **lui** offre un cadeau*. The person receiving is indirect, so the pronoun is *lui / leur*.

**Compare two countries.** *En France, on fête le 14 juillet avec un défilé, mais chez nous on ne le fête pas.* A comparison plus a direct object pronoun in one sentence.

**Close with an evaluation.** *Ce que j'aime le plus, c'est de voir toute la famille, parce qu'on ne se voit pas souvent.*

steps.title: Summary
steps.body:
- **Dates**: *le* + number + month, no capital; *le premier* for the 1st.
- Festivals: *le Nouvel An, Pâques, la fête nationale, la Toussaint, Noël, l'Aïd, un mariage, un anniversaire*.
- Verbs: *fêter, célébrer, organiser, inviter, **offrir*** (participle **offert**), *se réunir*.
- *Il y a* + noun: *un repas, un défilé, un feu d'artifice, des décorations*.
- Where: *chez ma grand-mère, chez nous, en ville*.
- **Custom → present**: *d'habitude, tous les ans, traditionnellement*.
- **Last year → perfect**: *l'année dernière, on est allés, j'ai reçu*.
- **This year → near future**: *cette année, on va inviter*.
- **Il y avait** and **c'était** for describing the past.
- *Des → de* after a negative.
- *Offrir à* → the pronoun is **lui / leur**.
- Compare: *en France … mais chez nous …*
- *Ce que j'aime le plus, c'est …*

examTechnique.body:
Give the date as **le** + number + month (with **le premier** for the 1st), place the celebration with **chez**, and list what happens with **il y a**.

The marks are in the **tense match**: *d'habitude* + present, *l'année dernière* + perfect, *cette année* + near future. Add **il y avait** and **c'était** to describe the past, shrink *des* to *de* after a negative, and close with an opinion and a reason.
examinerErrors: Le un janvier for the first.
À la maison de instead of chez.
C'est instead of c'était for last year.
J'offre ma sœur un cadeau without à.
Only one tense in the whole answer.
examTechnique.grade9Looks: A grade 9 answer writes every date correctly, then moves cleanly between three tenses, each announced by its marker — the custom in the present, last year in the perfect, this year in the near future. It sets the past scene with *il y avait* and judges it with *c'était*, places celebrations with *chez*, shrinks the article after negatives, uses *lui / leur* with *offrir*, and compares its own customs with French ones before closing on an evaluation.
